t: Find the error: "I told Rahul on wait for two hours at the bus stop."
o: told Rahul on wait for two hours
e: Imperatives in reported speech use 'to + V1' → "told Rahul to wait for two hours".

t: Find the error: "Had I known, I should have done things differently."
o: I should have done things differently
e: Inverted Type 3 follows the same 'would have' pattern → "I would have done things differently".

t: Find the error: "Monika said to her mother that, 'I have passed.'"
e: Direct speech after a reporting verb takes a comma, not 'that' → "said to her mother, 'I have passed.'"

t: Find the error: "Every Saturday, your mother prepares a pudding, isn't she?"
o: Every Saturday, your mother prepares a pudding
e: Simple present, third person needs 'doesn't' → "doesn't she?"

t: Find the error: "I imagine you have learnt a lot, didn't you?"
o: I imagine you have learnt a lot
e: The tag must match the auxiliary in the sentence (has/have) → "haven't you?"

t: Find the error: "He behaves if he were a king."
o: behaves if he were a king
e: The correct phrase for pretence is 'as if', not just 'if' → "behaves as if he were a king".

t: Find the error: "If it had not rained, they would not postpone the match."
o: they would not postpone the match
e: Type 3 main clause needs 'would have + V3' → "would not have postponed".

t: Find the error: "If she will exercise daily, she would remain energetic."
e: Type 1 conditional never has 'will' in the if-clause → "If she exercises daily".

t: Find the error: "Rahul's sister says that my brother is the best dancer in the city."
o: that my brother is the best dancer
e: Pronouns change according to the actual speaker → "that her brother is the best dancer".

t: Fill in the blank: If you had asked for directions, you would not ______ lost now.
e: Mixed conditional: past condition (had asked) + present result (would + V1 = be).

t: Find the error: "Rishi asked Karan will he get a new football."
o: will he get a new football
e: Yes/No questions in reported speech use 'if/whether' + statement order → "if he would get a new football".

t: Fill in the blank: If she ______ earlier, she wouldn't have missed the flight.
Find the error: "Let us work out the details, shouldn't we?"
o: Let us work out the details
e: 'Let us' proposals always take the tag 'shall we?' → "shall we?"

t: Find the error: "Rashmi works hard, don't she?"
e: Simple present with third-person singular needs 'doesn't' → "doesn't she?"

t: Fill in the blank: He behaves as if he ______ everything about the topic.
e: 'As if' for pretence takes past tense.
